title: Why Is the Floor of an F1 Car Worth Millions?
description:
The most expensive part of a Formula One car is one you will almost never see. It is not the engine and it is not the steering wheel. It is the floor, a flat sheet of carbon fibre under the car, so important that teams spend millions of dollars designing it and guard its shape like a state secret. Today, ten parts that make an F1 car stick to the track, and why each one exists, starting with the floor.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 10 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:18 1. The floor
2:54 2. The plank
4:23 3. The diffuser
5:46 4. The front wing
7:11 5. The rear wing flap
8:46 6. The bargeboards
10:03 7. The sidepods
11:30 8. The sliding skirts
12:55 9. The fan
14:19 10. The wind tunnel model
15:44 The verdict
